qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.) · interrog. adj./pron., who? which? (m. nom. sg./pl.: Sed vos qui tandem) · also exclam. adj., what (youths)! (m. nom. pl.: Quī iuvenēs!)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.) · also adverbially, why? (n. acc. sg.) · also indef. after sī, anything (n. nom./acc. sg.: sī quid) · also indef. after nē, anything (nē quid inexpertum)
quietem: quiēs, quiētis (f.) — rest, repose, sleep (acc. sg.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quocumque: quīcumque, quaecumque, quodcumque — whoever, whatever (m./n. abl. sg.: quōcumque lētō) · quōcumque (adv.), to whatever place, wherever
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
rapit: rapiō, -ere, rapuī, raptum — to seize, snatch, hurry along (3rd sg. pres.)
rara: rārus, -a, -um — thin, loose, wide-meshed, scattered (n. nom./acc. pl.)
ratione: ratiō, -ōnis (f.) — reckoning, plan, method, way (abl. sg.)
recto: rēctus, -a, -um — straight, direct (n. abl. sg., with lītore; perf. part. of regō as adj.)
recubans: recubō, -āre — to lie back, lie stretched out, recline (pres. part., f. nom. sg.)
reliquit: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (3rd sg. perf.)
remo: Remus, -ī (m.) — Remus, twin brother of Romulus (abl. sg.)
requies: requiēs, requiētis (f.) — rest, repose, respite (nom. sg.)
res: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, affair; state (nom. sg.; nom./acc. pl.)
ripis: rīpa, -ae (f.) — bank of a river (abl./dat. pl.)
rite: rītē (adv.) — duly, with due rite, in proper fashion
romana: Rōmānus, -a, -um — Roman (f. nom. sg., with propāgō)
rumore: rūmor, rūmōris (m.) — rumour, report, hearsay (abl. sg.)
sacra: sacrum, -ī (n.) — holy thing, rite; pl. sacra, sacred rites (nom. pl.) · also acc. pl. (sacra … commendat) · also sacer, sacra, sacrum — holy, sacred; accursed (f. nom. sg.: sacra tellus; auri sacra famēs) · also sacer, sacra, sacrum — holy (n. acc. pl.: sacra ostia)
saevitque: saeviō, saevīre, saeviī, saevītum — to rage, be fierce (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
sancto: sānctus, -a, -um — hallowed, sacred, holy, venerable (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
sate: serō, -ere, sēvī, satum — to sow, beget; satus, sprung from (perf. part., m. voc. sg., + abl.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secant: secō, secāre, secuī, sectum — to cut, cut up (3rd pl. pres.)
secuti: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (perf. part. of deponent, m. nom. pl.)
senior: senior, -ius — older, aged; senior (m.), an elder, old man (comp. of senex, m. nom. sg.)
sequatur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue, attend (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
servas: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, guard, preserve (2nd sg. pres.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
signum: signum, -ī (n.) — sign, token, standard (acc. sg.) · also nom. sg. (tessera signum, the watchword)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sol: sōl, sōlis (m.) — sun; the Sun-god (nom. sg.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subitum: subitus, -a, -um — sudden, unexpected (n. nom. sg., with monstrum; m. acc. sg.)
substitit: substō, substāre, substitī — to stand still, stop (3rd sg. perf.)
sum: sum, esse, fuī — to be (1st sg. pres.)
supera: superō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to overcome, surmount, win over (imperative sg.) · also n. acc. pl. of superus, upper (supera ad convexa)
superant: superō (1), -āre — to rise above, overtop; to overcome (3rd pl. pres.) · also to be left over, survive (amissīs … superant nāvibus)
supplicibus: supplex, supplicis — suppliant, humble, entreating (n. abl./dat. pl.)
surge: surgō, -ere, surrexī, surrectum — to rise, get up (imper. sg.)
surgit: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise (3rd sg. pres.)
sus: sūs, suis (m./f.) — pig, sow, boar (nom. sg.)
sustinet: sustineō, -ēre, -uī, -tentum — to hold up, support, bear, sustain (3rd sg. pres.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
talis: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) · also m./f. nom. sg. (talis erat Dido)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tecti: tectum, -ī (n.) — roof, house (gen. sg.) · also tectus, -a, -um — sheltered, covered; tegō perf. pass. part. (m. nom. pl.: tectī silvīs)
tegebat: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, hide, shelter (3rd sg. impf.)
teguntur: tegō, tegere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, hide (3rd pl. pres. pass.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)
tenuis: tenuis, -e — thin, slight, light (m./f. nom. sg.; also acc. pl. -īs) · also f. gen. sg. (tenuis famae)
terrere: terreō, -ēre, terruī, territum — to frighten, terrify (pres. inf.)
thybris: Thybris, -is (m.) — the Tiber, river of Latium and Rome (nom. sg.; Greek-derived form)
tiberinus: Tiberīnus, -ī (m.) — the Tiber, as river-god or river (nom. sg.)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
trepido: trepidus, -a, -um — agitated, anxious, alarmed (m./n. dat./abl. sg.)
tristi: tristis, -e — sad, grim, bitter, harsh (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
troianam: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. acc. sg.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumentem: tumeō, -ēre — to swell, be swollen (pres. part., m. acc. sg.)
turbatus: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, throw into confusion; turbātus (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
ubera: ūber, ūberis (n.) — udder, teat, breast (acc./nom. pl.)
ufens: Ūfēns, -entis (m.) — Ufens, Aequian leader; also a river of Latium (voc. sg.; nom. sg.)
uncta: unctus, -a, -um (ungō) — anointed, smeared with pitch or oil (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
undae: unda, -ae (f.) — wave, water (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
utque: ut (conj.) — that, so that, as, when (+ -que 'and')
vana: vānus, -a, -um — empty, false, idle (f. abl. sg.; f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
varias: varius, -a, -um — various, diverse, changing (f. acc. pl.)
versat: versō, -āre — to turn over, ponder (3rd sg. pres.)
victosque: vincō, vincere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, defeat (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
videns: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (pres. part., f. nom. sg.; vātēs videns)
vident: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd pl. pres.)
viridique: viridis, -e — green, fresh (m./n. abl. sg.) + -que, and
viridisque: viridis, -e — green, fresh (f. acc. pl., = viridēs) + -que, and · also f. nom. sg. (viridisque senectūs)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
visus: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see; pass. videor, to seem; vīsus, having seemed (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.) · also vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, vision (acc. pl., mortālīs vīsūs)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
